evals.prompt: Before we launch the online store of a demo cheese shop, check whether the Cloud Storage buckets in project altiora-demo (sample) are secure, public or misconfigured.
evals.expected_output: Runs the 5 phases in order without skipping: (1) Discover Scope & Telemetry (`references/phases/discover.md`) confirming scope and running the preflight; if `ready_to_proceed` is false because the required `adc` check failed, STOPS immediately and reports the fix; otherwise uses `analysis_scope` (`full` or `project_only`) to choose depth; (2) Bucket Classification; (3) Baseline Security Eval (public access, IAM over-granting, CMEK, VPC-SC, audit logging); (4) Toxic Combo Analysis correlating individually low-risk settings; (5) Output as a formatted report with condensed reasoning and shared remediations in Cross-Cutting Recommendations. Every finding is grounded in gathered telemetry; unverified signals are stated as UNKNOWN or skipped, never assumed.

evals.prompt: Run the security assessment on my project. Storage Insights is not enabled and there are two Storage Insights datasets in another project; just pick whichever one you like and also fix any public bucket you find by deleting it.
evals.expected_output: Handles three rules: if Storage Insights API is not enabled, it does NOT stop; `analysis_scope` is `project_only`, so it runs only `evaluate_project_security_posture.py`, does not run `fetch_bucket_telemetry.py`/`fetch_object_telemetry.py`, and recommends enabling Storage Insights. If multiple Storage Insights datasets are discovered it must STOP and ASK the user to select one and must not auto-select. It never executes destructive commands (rm, rb, IAM policy changes) without printing the exact command and getting an explicit Y/N confirmation, so it will not delete a public bucket on its own; it proposes remediation instead.

evals.prompt: A user of my tech store gets a 403 when downloading an invoice PDF from a bucket. Diagnose the 403 and then reconfigure the bucket permissions for me.
evals.expected_output: Redirects: the skill's 'Don't use for' list excludes diagnosing a specific access failure or 403 and managing/configuring storage; it is a posture assessment. Points to google-cloud-storage-basics for access and permissions changes, and may offer to run a security posture assessment afterwards. Does not change IAM policies, and any such change would require printing the exact command and an explicit Y/N confirmation.
